title: Butter Bean and Chorizo Stew
subtitle: Spanish-style smoky butter bean and chorizo braise
excerpt: A deeply warming one-pot stew: butter beans braised with cooking chorizo, smoked paprika, tomatoes, and spinach until the beans are silky and the chorizo has stained the broth a deep, smoky red.

recipe.sourceNotes: A Spanish-influenced one-pot stew combining butter beans with cooking chorizo, smoked paprika, and tomatoes. The dish draws on the tradition of Spanish potajes (bean stews) enriched with cured meats. Cooking chorizo (as opposed to cured slicing chorizo) releases its paprika-stained fat into the dish as it fries, which becomes the base for the whole stew. Butter beans are used here for their large size and silky texture when cooked; they absorb the spiced chorizo fat particularly well. Tinned butter beans are the practical choice; dried beans soaked and cooked from scratch produce an even better result if time allows.

content.text: Use cooking chorizo, not cured slicing chorizo; the cooking variety releases its fat when fried and this is the flavour base for the whole stew. Fry the chorizo first until it is browned and has released its oil, then use that oil to cook everything else. The spinach can be added frozen; it wilts into the stew without adding extra liquid.

items.preparation: two 400 g tins; drained and rinsed
cooking chorizo; sliced into 1 cm rounds

content.text: Fry the chorizo in a large pan over medium-high heat for 3 to 4 minutes until browned and the fat has run out. Remove with a slotted spoon, leaving the oil. Cook the onion in the chorizo fat for 5 minutes. Add the garlic and smoked paprika and cook for 1 minute.
Add the tinned tomatoes and stock. Bring to a simmer and cook for 10 minutes. Add the butter beans and return the chorizo. Simmer for 10 minutes until the sauce has thickened.
Add the spinach and stir until wilted. Add the sherry vinegar. Season. Scatter with parsley and serve with crusty bread.
